title: Store Catchment Area Calculator
description: Size a store's catchment with the Store Catchment Area Calculator — primary and secondary rings, areas and the population maths they feed. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a store's 3-mile primary catchment covers 28.3 square miles — at a suburban density of 2,500 people per square mile, that is roughly 70,700 potential customers before a single competitor is counted.
quick_answer: The Store Catchment Area Calculator sizes the rings a store draws its trade from — typically a primary ring, a secondary ring and an outer zone — computing each band's true area. Enter the ring radii and read the areas: the ground truth beneath catchment population estimates and site comparisons.

Ring area × local density = catchment population, labelled as the estimate it is. The calculator keeps the area exact so the estimate's softness lives only in the density.
A new store's rings over an existing store's: the shared bands' areas price the overlap before the opening does.
Catchment areas are the franchise brochure's honest core — computed rings, stated radii, no hand-waved 'greater metro area'.

Primary 0–2 mi: 12.6 sq mi. Secondary 2–5 mi: 66.0 sq mi. Outer 5–10 mi: 235.6 sq mi. The outer ring dwarfs the others — which is why trade percentages, not raw areas, run catchment thinking (the classic 60/25/15 split of customers by ring).
The same 28.3 sq mi primary ring holds ~70,700 people at 2,500/sq mi and ~7,100 at 250/sq mi. Area is exact; density is local. The calculator never lets the first disguise the second.
